subject: Performance SLO qualification: context window & latency targets
messages:
From: Alan Reeves <alan@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO qualification: context window & latency targets

Hi Marissa / Dylan,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough earlier — helpful to see the routing and fallback options. As discussed on the call, I wanted to capture our performance targets and a few open items so we can qualify Redwood for our proof-of-concept. High level:

- Workload: document ingestion + extractive Q&A over long contracts (mix of short and long prompts).
- Typical request: 4–6 documents concatenated (~8k–12k tokens input) with a 512–1024 token generated answer (often streamed to the UI).
- Concurrency: peak of ~120 concurrent sessions, average 60 sustained sessions during business hours.
- Throughput target: ~600 qps sustained across the cluster during peak (rough estimate based on concurrency + user cadence).
- Latency SLOs: we want p95 end-to-end latency <= 600ms for 512-token outputs when streaming is enabled; for non-streaming batch responses p95 <= 900ms.

Questions / asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm expected p95 token-latency for a 32k-context model variant (we discussed using a 32k-compatible open model) on dedicated capacity?
2) What concurrency/throughput limits do you expect per-GPU for the config you recommended?
3) Any special considerations for streaming (start-of-stream latency vs token cadence) that will affect perceived latency in our UI?
4) We'll provide representative payloads and traces — what format do you prefer?

I'll loop in procurement (cc'ed) to start the contracting conversation once we have a sense of sizing and pricing.

Thanks,
Alan Reeves
CTO, FinCo
alan@finco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alan Reeves <alan@finco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification: context window & latency targets

Alan — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers up front and a proposed next step list below. I've attached a short SLO questionnaire (SLO_questionnaire_v1.pdf) that captures the workload shape we'll use for baseline runs. If you can fill out the sample payloads section (example prompts + avg token counts) that'll speed things up.

Quick notes:
- Context window: our 32k-compatible variants use optimized KV cache and chunked attention so p95 token-latency does increase compared to 8k models, but with dedicated capacity and streaming we typically see p95 for the first-response-start in the 250–450ms range for outputs up to ~512 tokens (token cadence after start is streaming-dependent). For full non-streaming 512-token responses end-to-end p95 typically falls in the 600–900ms range depending on batching and request sizes.
- Per-GPU throughput: rough rule-of-thumb for the model family we discussed is ~60–100 concurrent low-latency streams per A100-class instance (depends on quantization & sequence length). For throughput-heavy batched workloads throughput per-GPU can be higher if you accept slightly higher p95. We'll provide a sizing sketch once we see your sample payloads.
- Streaming: there are two relevant metrics — time-to-first-byte (start latency) and sustained token cadence. We can prioritize lower start latency by reducing batching window and enabling prefetching, at the expense of some unit cost.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Alan: share 3 representative requests (raw prompt + expected output) and any traces you can share — prefer ndjson traces or simple JSON request/response samples.
2) Redwood: we'll run two baseline tests on Dedicated staging: (a) streaming-enabled test for your sample payloads, (b) non-streaming batch test. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, start-of-stream latency, and token cadence.
3) Procurement: once sizing is clear, we'll produce a dedicated capacity proposal and estimated monthly commit.
4) If results look good, propose a one-week pilot (dedicated slice) to validate with your actual traffic.

Attachments: SLO_questionnaire_v1.pdf

Let me know if you want to change any of the targets above. We can set up a short follow-up 30-min sync next week to review baseline test plans.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alan Reeves <alan@finco.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finco.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification: context window & latency targets

Thanks Marissa — attached are the sample payloads and a short synthetic trace to reproduce our most common heavy case.

Summary of the attached:
- payloads.json: three requests; avg input tokens 9,400, expected output 512 tokens (streamed).
- traces.tar.gz: client-side timing for start-of-request and perceived first-token latency.

Procurement — looping you in so we can get a ballpark commitment estimate after Redwood shares sizing. Two asks from our side: (1) ballpark monthly cost for the pilot (1-week dedicated slice) and (2) licensing/pricing model for production if we go to a reserved commit.

Alan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alan Reeves <alan@finco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification: context window & latency targets

Alan / team — got the payloads, thanks. We kicked off an initial baseline run on a staging dedicated slice and captured the following high-level observations (preliminary):

- Streaming start-of-response (p95) for your 9.4k-token inputs + 512-token outputs: ~420ms. Token cadence post-start averaged ~18–22 tokens/sec depending on batch window.
- Non-streaming end-to-end (full 512 tokens) p95: ~820ms.
- Observed per-GPU concurrency for low-latency streams (target config): ~75 concurrent streams on the instance we used before p95 degradation. For higher sustained throughput we recommend sharding across multiple GPUs with a routing policy we can configure.

Attachments: runbook_latencies.xlsx (contains the raw percentiles and run configs).

Preliminary recommendation:
- For the pilot (1-week dedicated slice) we'd provision a 4-GPU slice with the config used in the staging run. That should comfortably support your peak concurrency with headroom to tune batching. Estimated pilot cost: ~$9,500 for the week (includes dedicated staging infra + perf engineering support).
- For production reserved commit: we'll provide a formal quote, but the model above maps to a monthly commit roughly in the $30k–$45k/month range depending on redundancy and regional placement.

Next steps:
1) Procurement — if that pilot ballpark looks reasonable, we can raise an order form and scope the exact start date.
2) Technical — Marissa / Dev will schedule a 30-min tuning session next week to optimize batching and streaming windows (Doodle link: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/perf-tune).

Let me know if you want the raw run logs or an expanded latency breakdown by kernel (we can include that in the runbook).

Thanks,
Marissa
